sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: vision rules, transfer ages, practice minimums and road test vehicle rejection
Confusable pairs among test requirements, transfer rules and road test logistics, followed by continuation facts on health certification, voter records and vehicle rejection; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A02
Basic license applicants need 20/50 vision with or without corrective lenses, while CDL applicants need 20/40 in both eyes plus the ability to tell red, green and amber lights apart. [A02]
Why it matters: group screening; confusable basic versus CDL vision.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A02
Federal law and New Jersey rules require commercial drivers to file a CDL Holder Self-Certification form and, if applicable, a medical examiner's certificate completed by a federally certified medical examiner. [A02]
Why it matters: group screening; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A01
The knowledge test language list includes American Sign Language, but a state-approved interpreter for an unlisted language is arranged only after a failed attempt in an offered language and with at least two weeks' notice. [A01]
Why it matters: group knowledge test; confusable offered language versus interpreter.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A01
Once a foreign-language interpreter is secured, an MVC employee contacts the applicant with the appointment date and time, while for Deaf or Hard of Hearing applicants the MVC pays the knowledge-test interpreter fees after a payment voucher form. [A01]
Why it matters: group knowledge test; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A03
A transfer applicant aged 18 or older with a valid non-provisional license gets a four-year basic license, while one aged 17 to 18 gets a probationary license for one year under GDL rules. [A03]
Why it matters: group transfers; confusable adult versus teen transfer.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A03
Out-of-state transfer applicants may have the knowledge and road tests waived, but every out-of-country applicant must pass the knowledge test and vision screening. [A03]
Why it matters: group transfers; confusable out-of-state versus out-of-country.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A05
Before a road test appointment, GDL permit holders under 21 need six months and at least 50 supervised hours with 10 after dark, while those 21 and older need only three months. [A05]
Why it matters: group road test; confusable under twenty-one versus adult practice minimum.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec03-R08 | anchor: A04
Address changes reported to the MVC online or by mail are forwarded to the New Jersey Division of Elections, and you should contact your local Commissioner of Registration if no confirmation arrives. [A04]
Why it matters: group records; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec03-R09 | anchor: A04
Someone not doing a license or ID transaction can still register to vote or change a voting address through the New Jersey Division of Elections, which can mail an application. [A04]
Why it matters: group records; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec03-R10 | anchor: A06
A test vehicle registered in another state must meet that home state's insurance identification laws. [A06]
Why it matters: group road test; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec03-R11 | anchor: A06
During the road test an MVC examiner rides with the applicant in an off-road test area or on a public road course to confirm the applicant knows the rules and drives safely. [A06]
Why it matters: group road test; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec03-R12 | anchor: A07
Many applicants assume only their driving is graded, but the vehicle itself can cause a denial, and an examiner may refuse even an initial road test in an unsuitable or unsafe car. [A07]
Why it matters: group road test; misconception driving versus vehicle.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec03-R13 | anchor: A08
A vehicle that failed inspection is rejected unless the motorist brings the Vehicle Inspection Report from the inspection station, and a fast engine idle is rejected because speed control cannot be judged. [A08]
Why it matters: group vehicle rejection; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec03-R14 | anchor: A08
Seat belts are required on all vehicles manufactured after July 1, 1966, so missing belts get a test vehicle rejected. [A08]
Why it matters: group vehicle rejection; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec03-R15 | anchor: A08
Window tint on the driver or front door windows, missing interior or driver-door mirrors, broken or cracked glass, and doors or windows that will not work from inside all get a vehicle rejected. [A08]
Why it matters: group vehicle rejection; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec03-R16 | anchor: A08
Brakes must not fade or sink to the floorboard, the parking brake, brake lights and signal lights must work, and the interior must be reasonably clean. [A08]
Why it matters: group vehicle rejection; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec03-R17 | anchor: A08
For motorcycle and moped tests only, missing state-required equipment, no helmet, unapproved goggles or face shield, or no bell or horn audible at 100 feet also cause rejection. [A08]
Why it matters: group vehicle rejection; scope note motorcycle and moped only.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0039]
